newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BONDS DOWN AT START, FURTHER FALLS EXPECTED.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BONDS DOWN AT START, FURTHER FALLS EXPECTED.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened lower on Monday, hit by Friday's Wall Street decline and dealers saw further falls in a market nervous about upcoming U.S. data.
"The correction seems set to continue, given last week's Wall Street falls and market jitters about Wednesday's U.S. July retail sales and production price data," one dealer warned.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 down 0.13 point from Friday's close at 112.32 with the yield at 6.10 percent. The seven percent 2007 paper, due to be benchmark on September 1, was 0.16 lower at 105.19, yielding 6.29 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one point from Friday to 59 bps.
The crown traded at an unchanged 3.8080 per mark at 0735 GMT.
